text:
They want to know how to say a word in another language.
How do you say dessert in Spanish?
Spanish word for cake, please
what's French for good morning
Can you translate this word into Italian for me?
I need the German words for double chocolate
How would I say the food is ready in Japanese?
Say come here in Portuguese, but make it short
What do people say in Korean when they want more rice?
I'm going to a dinner party and would love to know how to tell my host that everything looks great, so could you put that into Turkish for me?

Sam woke up late, with his hair going in every direction, and walked into the kitchen with his eyes half shut. He mumbled to the phone on the counter, "Plan dinners for the week and put the shopping list on my screen." The assistant sounded bright and calm. It said it had planned five dinners: pasta, soup, rice with beans, tacos and baked fish. It had also made a shopping list with everything those meals need. Sam asked for the list to be short, so the assistant took off things he already had at home, like salt and oil. Then Sam said he only had one hour on Sunday to cook. The assistant moved the soup and the rice to Sunday, because both could be made in an hour and kept in the fridge. It all felt smooth, almost like magic. Sam yawned, thanked the phone, and poured his coffee. The list was already waiting on his screen.

They want a good place to go cycling.
Where can I bike near here?
Find me a short loop for tonight
I want a flat route, nothing with big hills
What's a nice path for a slow ride after yoga class?
Name a few bike trails by the river, please
Give me about ten miles, easy pace
Somewhere safe for my kid to cycle
Could you please suggest a route that is not too long and has street lights, because it gets dark early now and I don't want to be out on a black road?

Dana was a busy parent with two kids and a long list of errands. Standing at the front door with her keys, she said to her phone, "Remind me to go to the post office, but don't put it before the market, because the market closes early." The assistant understood that the post office had to come after the market. It made a list of stops in that order: market, bank, post office. Dana said she did not want any stop on the list after five, since the kids needed dinner. The assistant checked the opening hours and told her the post office closed at five thirty, so she could still make it. It marked the bank as done after she said she had paid the bill online, and that left only two stops. Dana smiled, picked up her bag, and herded the kids toward the car. The reminders were set.

Luca was a cook in a small restaurant, and tonight a guest from Japan was sitting at the front table. His hands were covered in flour, so he spoke to the speaker on the shelf. "Tell me how to say welcome in Japanese and write it on a card for the table." The assistant said the word slowly, twice, so Luca could copy the sounds. Then it wrote the word on his screen in big letters. Luca also asked it to filter out the hard words and keep only easy ones, so the assistant gave him three simple phrases: thank you, please eat, and enjoy. Luca practiced while he stirred the soup. When the guest heard his greeting, she laughed with joy. Later she said the warm welcome was the best prize of her whole trip.

A contact list is a small book inside your phone. It is for finding people fast, so you do not have to remember every phone number or address. Each contact can hold a name, a number, an email, a home address and a birthday. People change their contacts all the time. When a friend moves, you say, update Ana's address, or change her number to the new one. When you meet someone new, you say, add a contact called Tom. If you want to remember a birthday, you say, put Mom's birthday on her card. On a foggy morning, a delivery driver may call you, and you can see the name instead of a strange number. Some people even dress up the list by giving each friend a small picture.

A weather forecast tells you what the sky will probably do, so you know what to wear and whether to take an umbrella. It is for small plans, like a walk, a picnic, or hanging washing on a rope outside. The forecast changes through the day. When the wind shifts, rain can come sooner than planned. People ask about it in many ways. They say, will it rain tomorrow, is it cold outside, or do I need a jacket. They can also ask for a different place, like what's the weather in Lima, or a different time, like what about Saturday. The final answer is simple: a number for the temperature and a word like sunny, windy or wet. Checking before you leave the house takes only a second.

Priya, an office worker, came home tired and saw the electric bill on the table. She was careful with money, so she spoke politely to the smart speaker. "Could you please show me how much electricity we used this week, because I think the heater uses too much and I would like to find out before the bill gets bigger?" The assistant said it understood she wanted her power use for the last seven days and a hint about the heater. It found the numbers and told her the heater had used nearly half of all the power. Priya wondered if an old wire behind the TV was wasting power too. The assistant said it could not see wires, but the numbers showed the heater was the big user. Priya asked it to remind her to turn the heater down at bedtime, and the assistant set a reminder for ten o'clock.

Jin was an office worker, and at lunch she sat on a chair in the park with a salad she had just chopped. The sun was so bright that she could not see her phone. "I can't see anything on here," she said. The assistant understood that she wanted the screen to be brighter, so it turned the brightness up. Now she could look at her photos. "These pictures look so dark," she said. The assistant took that to mean she wanted them lighter, and it offered to fix the light on the last photo. Jin said yes. The picture of her sister's garden became clear and warm. She was glad, and she asked the assistant to send it to her sister. The assistant sent the photo and told Jin it had been delivered.

Birthdays come once a year, and it is easy to forget the date. Many people keep a list of the birthdays of friends and family, with a number for each person's age. A phone can show a small note a few days before, so you have time to buy a gift or send a card. When you want to change something, you say, remind me a week before Dad's birthday, or add Grace's birthday on March ninth. If you need an idea, you can ask, what is a good gift for a grandmother, or find me something under twenty dollars. A tiny gift with a nice note can make someone very happy. After the party, some people follow up with a thank you message.

name: print_copies
does: Prints a chosen file or scanned page and makes as many copies as you ask for.
inputs: the file or page to print, how many copies, and which printer
people say:
- make ten copies of this
- I need the snow trip photo on paper
- print the recipe for salty pretzels twice
- can you multiply this page so everyone gets one
- run off five more of the flyer
- print both sides of the class list

name: reading_time_left
does: Tells how long it will take to finish a book or a chapter at the reader's usual speed.
inputs: the book title, the page or chapter you are on, and your reading speed if you know it
people say:
- how long until I finish this book
- will I be done before bed
- how many minutes is this chapter
- this book has real weight, how many hours is it
- it's a snowy day and I want to finish my novel, how long will that take
- I'm wearing my reading glasses, how much is left of this chapter

Ben was a child with a little jar of coins and a big wish for a new toy. He asked the tablet on the table, "How much money have I got? Don't count the coins from my sister." The assistant understood that it should count only Ben's coins. It added up the money he had told it about before and said he had twelve dollars. The toy cost twenty. The assistant said he needed eight more dollars. Ben did not want to ask his parents, so he asked how he could save it. The assistant said that if he put away two dollars every week, he could have the toy in four weeks. Ben asked it to switch on a weekly reminder, and the assistant set it for Sunday morning. That night Ben could sleep well, because he had a plan.

Omar was an office worker who worked from home on Thursdays. His wifi kept dropping, and he did not want to call anyone about it. "Restart the router tomorrow at seven in the morning, before my first meeting," he said to his phone. The assistant understood that he wanted the router to switch off and on at seven the next day. It said it could do that and set the time. Omar also asked it to check the local network, and the assistant found that the signal was weak in his room. It suggested moving the router closer, or choosing a different route for the cable. Omar said he would move it tonight. The next morning at seven the router restarted by itself, and the wifi was fast again when he sat down to work.

They want to know how much power the house has used.
How much electricity did we use yesterday?
Power use this week?
What's our total for the month so far?
Show me how much energy the house burned since Monday
Was last night a good night for saving power, or did we use a lot?
Tomorrow at seven, tell me how much we used overnight
Can you give me the numbers for the last three days, please?
I just got the broom out of the closet and saw every light on, so how much power has gone to waste today?

Units are the names we give to measures, like inches, meters, pounds and degrees. Cooks use cups and spoons. A person who builds a drawer uses a tape with centimeters on it. Friends in different countries often use different units, so they need to change from one to the other. People share a recipe and say, how many grams is a cup of flour, or what is seventy degrees in Celsius. They also ask, how long is five miles in kilometers, or give that to me in inches instead. It can get noisy in a busy kitchen, so a quick answer is nice. The point of a unit is that everyone agrees how big a thing is, and that you can say it the same way twice.

A baby needs food and sleep at regular times. Parents often keep a little schedule: feed at six, nap at nine, feed again at noon. A schedule helps everyone know what is next, but it is never exactly correct, because babies do not read the clock. If the baby sleeps longer on a Tuesday, the parent moves the next feed later. People say, push the nap by thirty minutes, or let her sleep a little more. They also say, remind me when it's time to feed him, or tell me when he wakes up. A baby monitor lets parents hear or see the room while they cook or rest. When the baby cries, the monitor tells the parent right away.

They want the air in a room to feel less hot.
Turn on the fan
It feels like I'm sitting in an oven in here
I don't want it this hot, please
Cool down the bedroom, but don't make it freezing
Is it true that the living room is warmer than the kitchen? Fix that
I can't even bathe in this heat without feeling sticky, so put the air conditioner on
Could you please chill the house a bit, not too much, because the baby is napping and I don't want her to get cold?

Marco, a cook, finished the lunch rush and looked out the window. The sky was gray, and the wind was blowing hard. "I was hoping for a long ride on my bike this afternoon," he said to his phone, "but it looks like it's about to pour." The assistant understood that he wanted to know if rain was coming. It checked and said rain would start at three. Marco said, "Then I'll skip the long one." The assistant found a short route of five kilometers that he could finish before three, and it saved the route as a document in his files. Marco had planned a ride with a friend, so he asked the assistant to undo that plan. It removed the event from his calendar and sent the friend a short message. Marco put on his helmet and left for his short ride.

A calendar helps you remember what happens on which day. It holds meetings, dentist visits, birthdays, and the quiet time you keep free for yourself. You can look at one day, one week, or the whole month. Plans change a lot, so people often ask for changes. They say, move my meeting to Friday, push lunch back an hour, or cancel the dentist. To add something new, they say, put a hike up the mountain on Saturday morning, or I'm going to the doctor at four tomorrow. They can also ask, am I free on Monday, or what do I have today. A good calendar tells you when two things happen at the same time, so you do not double book.

They want to know the total of two numbers.
twenty-five plus seventeen
What's 25 and 17 together?
Add up twenty-five and seventeen for me
I bought a yellow shirt for twenty-five and a hat for seventeen, how much was that in all?
I have a discount coupon for seventeen dollars and another for twenty-five, so how much do the two give me?
Before the wind blows my receipt away, what is twenty-five plus seventeen?
Could you kindly tell me what you get when you join twenty-five to seventeen?
Seventeen and twenty-five, total?

A text message is a short note you send from your phone. People use texts when a call is too much or when the other person might be asleep. You write it, pick who gets it, and send it. A group chat lets many people read the same thread, like a family chat with your mother, your brother and your aunt. When a new message comes, the phone buzzes or wakes the screen. People say, text Sam that I'm late, read my new messages, or reply yes to Dad. If you do not have enough time to type, you can say the words and the phone writes them. If you made a mistake, you can say, change that to six o'clock.

Hana had just moved to a new city and did not know the shops yet. Her coworker's birthday was on Friday, and she wanted to give a gift. Standing at a shop window, she asked her phone, "What can I give a coworker? I don't want anything pricey or anything with flowers." The assistant understood that she needed gift ideas with a small price and no flowers. It pulled up a few: a nice mug, a box of tea, and a notebook. It also showed which shops near her were open. Hana picked the tea and asked for a card to go with it. The assistant said a paper shop was two streets away. It set a reminder for Thursday so her gift would be ready on time. Hana walked there feeling less lost.

Music on a phone or speaker works like a radio you control. You pick a song, an artist or a playlist, and it plays. A playlist is a list of songs that someone saved together. People make one for a party, for a run, or for a quiet evening. While a song plays, they change things. They say, turn it down, skip this one, play the last song again, or louder, please. In a car, a driver with a foot on the brake might ask for music, and a soft beep from the speaker shows it understood. When a favorite song starts, people are glad and ask for it again. You can also say, add this to my road trip list.

name: bin_day_check
does: Tells which bin goes out on a given day and what can go in it.
inputs: the street or home address, and the item or day you are asking about
people say:
- when does the truck come for my street
- does this pizza box go in recycling
- my bin is full and I could cry, when is the next pickup
- what do I do with the little bottles from the hotel
- I need to know fast if glass goes in the green bin

name: nap_tracker
does: Writes down when the baby falls asleep and wakes up, and tells how long each nap was.
inputs: the baby's name, and the time the nap started or ended
people say:
- the baby just fell asleep
- she's awake now
- how long did he sleep today
- the room is dark and he's finally quiet, write it down
- I want to understand how much she sleeps, show me this week
- save this nap, I'll put it on the clinic website later

Many older people take medicine at set times, and a reminder helps them take the correct pill at the right hour. A family member can ask a phone or speaker to remind Grandma at eight and again at noon. Some people keep a notebook by the bed with the list of pills and the doctors' numbers. Check-in calls are short calls made every day to hear that everything is fine. If something goes wrong, an emergency button can call a family member or bring help. People say, remind Dad to take his pills at nine, call Mom now, change the reminder to ten, or tell me if she did not answer. These small things give families peace of mind.

A podcast is a show you listen to, with a new episode every week. An audiobook is a book read aloud and split into chapters. Both remember where you stopped, so you can pick up again later. Many apps move to the next episode automatically. People listen while they cook, drive or walk, and sometimes a grandfather listens in the garden. To control it, they say, play the next episode, go back thirty seconds, or skip this chapter. If a voice is too slow, they say, play it faster, or one and a half times speed. If they swipe the wrong thing on the phone, they can say, take me back to where I was. Saying, where did I leave off, tells you the chapter and the minute.

They want to know when their team plays.
When is the next game?
Game time?
Is there a match tonight?
When do the Tigers play next?
Does the game start tomorrow at seven?
My fingers freeze at the stadium, so what time should I get there?
What's the current schedule for my team? I want to watch before the cake comes out of the oven.
Could you please tell me when my team plays next, because I'd like to invite friends over and need to plan the food?

They want to know how many days are left until a date.
How many days until Christmas?
Days left till my trip
Count down to Friday
How many sleeps until my birthday on June third?
How many days and hours until next Monday at nine?
It's nice out and I'm cleaning the garage, so how long until the party on Saturday?
Reset my countdown and tell me how many days are left until the exam on the fifth
Could you tell me how much time remains before my sister lands on the twelfth?

name: parking_timer
does: Starts a timer for the time left on a parking spot and warns you before it runs out.
inputs: how long you paid for and the time you parked
people say:
- remind me before the meter runs out
- I parked at two for two hours, tell me when to go back
- how much time is left on my spot
- I love this shop but I always forget my car, ring me ten minutes early
- I'm wearing my apron at work and can't watch the clock, keep an eye on the meter
- I only need a medium stop, about an hour, so set a timer

Elena was a nurse who had just finished a night shift. She came home and sat by the hot tub in the yard under a grey morning sky. She put a hand in the water and said, "Brr, it's not warm at all, and I have an appointment for my sore back at noon." The assistant understood that she wanted the water to be hotter. It asked if she wanted it hot right away, and Elena said yes, but not too hot. The assistant started the heater and set it to thirty-eight degrees. It said the water would be ready in about forty minutes. Elena asked it to remind her at eleven so she would not miss the appointment, and the assistant set the reminder. She went inside to eat breakfast, and later she slid into the warm water.

Parking is about finding a safe place to leave your car and paying for the time you use. Many streets have a meter or an app. You type your plate number, pick how long to stay, and pay. Some people upload a photo of the ticket to prove they paid. In the early morning the street is silent and spots are easy to find, but at noon they are not. If you want more time, you say, add thirty minutes to my parking, or how much time is left. People also ask, where can I park near the market, or is parking free on Sundays. On a hot day, a shady spot is nice, since a car is no place to bathe in sunshine.

Kofi was a driver, and the road ahead was long and heavy with traffic. At a red light he said to the car, "Play the next episode of my cooking show, but don't start it from the beginning." The assistant understood that he wanted to continue where he left off, not start over. It found the show, said he had stopped at minute twenty-two, and began from there. A little later, the host talked about a train trip through the mountains, and Kofi laughed. When a call came in, the assistant paused the show, and when it ended he asked, "Where was I?" The assistant went back thirty seconds and played again. Kofi said he did not want the sound so loud, and the assistant lowered the volume. At a gas station he stopped to stretch his legs, and the assistant kept the show paused.

Rosa owned a flower shop. She stood on a ladder hanging a sign when her phone buzzed. Her sister was flying in that afternoon. "Check if my sister's flight is on time and text her that I will pick her up," Rosa said to the assistant, without climbing down. The assistant understood two things: look up the flight, and send a message. It told Rosa the plane was running twenty minutes late and would land at four forty. Then it sent the text to her sister, saying Rosa would meet her at the arrivals door. Rosa thanked it. Several customers came in, so she asked for a reminder at four to leave for the airport. The assistant set it. Rosa climbed down and went back to work, glad that she did not have to look at the airport board herself.

Notes are small pieces of writing that help you remember things. You can type them or say them as voice notes. People write a shopping list with cheese on it, an idea for a gift, or a rough estimate of what a repair will cost. A clean list is easy to read later, so people tidy their notes. To make a new note, they say, write down call the plumber, or start a note called trip ideas. To find old notes, they say, find my note about the garden. To change a note, they say, add milk to my list, or cross off eggs. If you no longer need it, you say, delete that note.

Kai was a teenager lying on the couch, texting with friends about a camping trip in the hills on Saturday. With one thumb he typed to his phone, "What's the weather like up there, and how cold will it get at night?" The assistant said the days would be about twenty degrees and the nights about five. Kai wrote, "Make me a packing list for two nights." The assistant made one: tent, sleeping bag, warm jacket, flashlight, water and snacks. Kai said his flashlight was not working, so the assistant added new batteries to the list. His friends jumped into the chat with thumbs-up. Kai asked the assistant to send the list to the whole group, and it did.

Tomas was a driver on an early run, and the cold morning made his eyes heavy. He did not want to rush, so he waited patiently at a red light and said to the car, "I am so sleepy, and I have a long road ahead." The assistant understood that he wanted something to wake him up. It found a coffee shop on the road, five minutes away, and asked if he wanted it strong. Tomas said strong, with a little sugar. The assistant sent the order ahead and told him it would be ready at the window. Tomas also asked it to remind him to buy a jar of jam for his mother on the way home, and the assistant added that to his list for the evening.

Lena was a busy parent working at her laptop while the kids watched a movie. She said to the assistant, "Create a new folder called School Forms on my desktop. No, wait, put it inside Documents." The assistant understood the correction and made the folder in Documents, not on the desktop. Then Lena asked it to move the three files about the school trip into the folder. The assistant moved them and said the folder had three files now. A moment later, the lid of the laptop was half closed and the screen went dark. The battery was low. Lena asked, "How much battery do I have left?" The assistant said twelve percent. She plugged in the charger. On the TV, the kids were watching a movie about a plane, and she smiled.

name: gift_idea_finder
does: Suggests gift ideas for a person based on their age, what they like and how much you want to spend.
inputs: who the gift is for, their interests, and a price limit
people say:
- what should I get my dad for his birthday
- I need a present for a ten-year-old who loves bikes
- something nice under thirty dollars
- my aunt is always in pain from her back, so what would show her I care
- ideas for a friend who lives near me and likes baking
- gifts for a person who has everything

Errands are the small jobs you do outside your home or desk, like mailing a letter, going to the bank or picking up a parcel. A post office or a bank is open only at certain hours, so people check before they go. A busy person plans the stops in a sensible order, with heavy things last so nothing gets in the way. People say, what time does the post office close, plan my errands for the afternoon, remind me to pick up the package, or take the bank off my list. When they finish one, they say, mark that done. Small fixes at home, like a dripping faucet, go on the list too, with a note to call someone.

They want to know where their package is.
Where's my parcel?
Track my package
Package status?
Has my order shipped yet?
Connect me to the tracking page for my order
Set an alarm for when the parcel arrives
That box is high priority for me, so tell me how far away it is
Could you tell me if the parcel I ordered last week has left the warehouse? I've been waiting a long time.

They want to divide a number into equal parts.
Split 120 by 4
What is one hundred twenty divided by four?
120 over 4 people?
How much does each person pay if four people share a large bill of 120?
Divide 120 four ways and repeat the answer slowly
If the people at dinner tonight at eight all pay the same, what is a quarter of 120?
Could you please work out what 120 comes to when it's cut into four equal shares?

They want to know what food is in the house.
Fridge check
What's in the fridge?
Do we have milk?
What have we got left to eat?
List the food in the kitchen
I'm angry at myself for forgetting, did we run out of eggs again?
Before I weigh the flour for baking, do we have enough sugar?
My son plays on the game console all day and eats everything, so what snacks are left?

Person: I'm going on a trip and I want to know if my money will go far there. How much is a hundred dollars?
Assistant: Which currency do you want to compare it with?
Person: Pounds. I'd like to show the kids what things cost.
Assistant: Today a hundred dollars is about seventy-nine pounds.
Person: That's less than I hoped. What about double that?
Assistant: Two hundred dollars is about one hundred fifty-eight pounds.
Person: Good. Can you send the money to my sister so she can mix it in with her trip money?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't send money. I can only tell you the rates and keep a safe note of them.

They want to know how much longer something must stay in the oven.
How much longer for the cake?
Time left on the bake
The top is still pale, how long should it stay in?
My cookies are not set in the middle yet, when will they be done?
Tell me when the loaf is ready to come out
The cream on top is still wet, so how much more time does it need?
The kitchen smells great, but I think the cake isn't done, so when should I check it again?
I have to pack up for the party at six, so how much longer does the bread need?

They want to tell the delivery driver where to leave a parcel.
leave the parcel at the front door
ask the driver to put it by the gate
Please have them leave the box next to the recycling bins, not at the door
leave my pakage with the neighbor
I need it early, can you ask them to come before nine?
Put a note on my order: no signature, just drop it
Could you please send a note to the driver? I'm out all day and I need the box left with the doorman.

name: group_speakers
does: Joins two or more speakers so they play the same music, or splits them back into separate ones.
inputs: which speakers to join, or which group to divide
people say:
- play the music in every room
- put the kitchen and the living room together
- I want the song on the balcony speaker too
- divide the speakers back into single rooms
- keep the sad movie music in the bedroom only
- make the whole house play at once

Nina was a busy parent standing at the park while her daughter played on the swings. She was nervous, because the school nurse had called twice and she had missed both calls. She said to her phone, "Call the school back, and turn the volume up a lot more, I can't hear anything over the kids." The assistant understood she wanted to call the school and make the sound louder. It raised the volume to full and dialed. The nurse said her son had a cold and had sneezed all morning, and he needed to go home. Nina asked the assistant to put the call on speakerphone so she could carry her bag. Then she asked it to text her husband to pick up the boy, since he was closer. Her husband wrote back that he was on his way, and Nina let out a long breath.

Jo was a teenager with a sore tooth. At breakfast, with a bowl of cereal going soggy, he texted his phone, "book me a dentist this week, but not on wednesday, i have a test." The assistant understood that it should find a visit on any day except Wednesday. It checked the clinic near his house and told him there were openings on Tuesday at four and Thursday at ten. Jo said he did not want to miss school, so he chose Tuesday at four. The assistant booked it and put it in his calendar. Jo asked it to tell him the clinic's opening hours too. It said they opened at eight and closed at six. Jo sent back a thumbs-up and ate his cereal on the other side of his mouth.
